note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on Tuesday 5 May 1936 and there was no contest in any division: the Unionists nominated for the 21 divisions in which they held majorities and the Nationalists for ten, and the retiring members for the divisions without a nomination were deemed re-elected (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9; Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5). Polling in County Tyrone was fixed for Wednesday 3 June 1936; no poll was needed. The new council first met on Monday 8 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 13 June 1936, p. 5). Henry Myles was returned unopposed for Gortin in place of John Turner, one of the changes printed with the division. The Mid-Ulster Mail and Belfast News-Letter print the name as H. Miles; the Ulster Herald prints Henry Myles (U.), and Henry Myles was elected to the Regional Education and County Library committees at the first meeting. Returned unopposed.
